title: Containers, Images, and Virtual Machines: Practical Comparison knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the central idea of “Containers, Images, and Virtual Machines: Practical Comparison”?
options: Treat tags as labels that can move and use a digest when an immutable content identity is required.
Assume a mutable tag always identifies identical bytes forever.
Commit registry credentials into the source repository.
Remove all previous release images before testing a new one.
questions.answer_key: Treat tags as labels that can move and use a digest when an immutable content identity is required.
questions.explanation: Tags are convenient for humans; content digests and release procedures improve repeatability and rollback confidence.

questions.prompt: For a lab covering containers, images, and virtual machines: practical comparison, what is the strongest evidence of learning?
options: Assume the command is portable and skip reading its output.
Make several unrelated changes before collecting a baseline.
Use a production host so the result looks realistic.
Record the command or configuration, predicted result, observed evidence, and one relevant edge case.
questions.answer_key: Record the command or configuration, predicted result, observed evidence, and one relevant edge case.
questions.explanation: A useful lab connects a predicted result to actual output and checks an edge case. This is safer and more reproducible than assuming success.

questions.prompt: If an example related to containers, images, and virtual machines: practical comparison fails, which response is best?
options: Disable permissions or security controls until the example works.
Trust the image tag without inspecting the image or version.
Reproduce the issue, inspect state/logs/configuration, test one hypothesis at a time, and verify the fix.
Delete every stopped container and unused volume before investigating.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the issue, inspect state/logs/configuration, test one hypothesis at a time, and verify the fix.
questions.explanation: The evidence-led approach keeps the diagnosis reproducible and avoids hiding the cause. For containers, images, and virtual machines: practical comparison, verify the fix with the exact setting or command that failed.
